newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rise in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rise in latest week.

text.p: The number of people filing new claims for unemployment benefits in early June rose by 1,000, the government said Thursday, far exceeding economists expectations.
The Labour Department said 339,000 people filed first-time claims for unemployment insurance benefits in the week ended June 7, up from 338,000 in the previous week.
Wall Street econmomists had forecast initial jobless claims would fall to 326,000 in the June 7 week.
The four-week moving average for claims -- considered a better gauge of labour market conditions than the weekly number -- rose to 329,500 in the latest week from 324,000 the previous week.

Total benefit rolls rose 30,000 to reach 2.306 million in the week ended May 31, the latest period for which those figures were available. That was up from 2.276 million the prior week, the department said.
Six states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 31, the latest period for which the data were available.
They were California, with 5,139 fewer initial claims, Georgia, down 1,718, New York, off 1,691, Viginia down 1,268, Florida off 1,239, and Pennsylvania, with 1,202 fewer claims.

California cited fewer layoffs because of the Memorial Day holiday-shortened work week, while Georgia had fewer layoffs in manufacturing. Virginia reported fewer layoffs in the fabricated metals industry. New York had no comment.
Florida reported fewer job losses in the construction, trade, service and transportation industries and manufacturing. Pennsylvania had few layoffs in the construction, trade and apparel industries.
There were no states reporting increases in claims exceeding 1,000, on an unadjusted basis, in the May 31 week.
